topic: Square-root function with a quadratic radicand: other x-intercept
problem: Let h(x)=-sqrt(x^2+bx+c). Its graph passes through (3,0) and (0,-sqrt(366)). If its other x-intercept is m, what is the greatest possible value of m?

bad.why: Solving x^2-125x+366=0 with the quadratic formula is heavy arithmetic after deriving b by hand; the graph shows the other x-intercept.

algebraFirst.description: Squares h(0) to get c=366, substitutes x=3 into the radicand to get b=-125, then factors x^2-125x+366 or uses the quadratic formula.

explanationNotes: Explain that h is zero exactly where the expression under the square root is zero, and that h(0)=-sqrt(c) tells us c=366. Fit b from the root at x=3, then click the radicand's other x-intercept, 122.
notes: Paraphrase of Bedrock Prep hard Problem 8, Radical Models. Since h(0)=-sqrt(c), c=366. Since h(3)=0, 9+3b+366=0 so b=-125. Radicand x^2-125x+366 factors as (x-3)(x-122); the larger x-intercept is 122. Explain why h=0 precisely when the radicand is 0. Category index: https://www.bedrockprep.com/problems
